title: Georgia State's AdmitHub text-message chatbot Pounce lifts on-time enrollment 3.3 percentage points in a randomized field experiment (AERA Open 2017)
summary: Page and Gehlbach's field experiment at Georgia State University: students assigned to AdmitHub's conversational AI assistant Pounce were 3.3 points more likely to enroll on time.
account: Lindsay Page and Hunter Gehlbach tested Pounce, an artificially intelligent text-message assistant developed by AdmitHub for Georgia State University (GSU), in a field experiment. It involved GSU-committed students during the summer before college, when tasks such as financial-aid paperwork cause “summer melt”. Their AERA Open article (volume 3, issue 4, October 2017; online 12 December 2017 per Crossref) reports treated students exhibited greater success with pre-enrollment requirements. They were 3.3 percentage points more likely to enroll on time, with enrollment impacts comparable to prior interventions but substantially reduced burden on university staff. In a Brookings piece of 11 September 2018 the two researchers describe the chatbot as answering many questions automatically with machine-learning algorithms. A small fraction goes to counselors. WABE reported on 14 June 2018 that GSU uses Pounce to answer students' questions. The date observed is the article's online publication date. The sources do not state the summer in which the experiment ran or the number of students.
purpose: Pounce was deployed to guide admitted students through pre-enrollment tasks. Higher on-time enrollment is that purpose.
system: Pounce, AdmitHub conversational AI text-message assistant for Georgia State University
segment: College transition support for admitted students

ratings.reason: General benefit without an individually attributable event: treated students were 3.3 percentage points more likely to enroll on time (ERIC abstract; Brookings).
General benefit without an event: the abstract reports enrollment impacts comparable to prior interventions with substantially reduced burden on university staff.

ai_role.statement: The chatbot delivered personalized reminders and answered questions automatically, routing only a small fraction to counselors (Brookings). The authors compare the effect to earlier human-delivered outreach. So the gain is in scale and staff burden as much as in the AI itself.

later.note: GSU's research partnership with Mainstay (formerly AdmitHub) continued; two later randomized trials of course-specific Pounce chatbots in introductory courses raised the share of students earning a B or higher by 5-6 percentage points and reduced course drops.
later.quote: We find the academic chatbot significantly shifted students’ final grades, increasing the likelihood students received a course grade of B or higher by 5-6 percentage points and reduced the likelihood students dropped the course.
